maria: CI build of redwood-ruby sampleapp failing with 401 from our private gem host during `bundle install`. Works locally. Anyone seen this in Docker-based CI?

kevin: Usually a build vs runtime creds issue. Are you running `bundle install` during `docker build`?

maria: Yes, Dockerfile runs `bundle install` during build. We mount .netrc as a secret at runtime, not at build time. Error: `Fetch https://gems.example.com/api/v1/dependencies?gems=redwood-ruby - 401 Unauthorized`.

jen: That explains it. If the netrc isn't present at build time Bundler can't auth. Quick unblock: pin Bundler to 2 in the Docker build (`gem install bundler -v 2.4.11`) — matched Maria's local environment and CI passed.

maria: Pinning worked. I'll open a tiny PR to update the sampleapp README with the build-time credential note and add one-line workflow check.

kevin: In the PR add a short snippet about the env var encoding pattern (e.g., `BUNDLE__GEMS__EXAMPLE__COM`) since that trips people. Also suggest using build-arg or temporary copy of netrc during build for secure CI.

jen: Agreed. Keep PR minimal: README note + workflow tweak. I'll review.

ci-bot: CI run 2125550026: rubygem/quickstart build rerun -> success :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks all — PR opened and assigned to @jen/@kevin.
